00The miss, owned

Why this paper didn't surface in the first prior-art pass — and the process fix.

The prior-art pass anchored on the well-known LLM-for-science cluster — Coscientist, ChemCrow, ProtoCode, BioPlanner, OpentronsAI — and never ran a targeted query on the two axes where PRISM actually lives: (a) digital-twin / simulation-in-the-loop validation of lab protocols and (b) multi-agent protocol refinement. There was also no completeness pass asking "what class of system would I have missed?" That is a process gap, not a knowledge gap — and it is the reason the equipment, GPU-simulation, and replication-metric legs below were each run as an explicit sweep whose every citation was then attacked by an independent reference-checker before it was allowed into this document.

01What PRISM actually is

Grounded in the paper's own text, not summary memory.

PRISM ("Protocol Refinement through Intelligent Simulation Modeling") turns a target experiment — they benchmark PCR amplification and Cell Painting — into an OT-2 / multi-instrument protocol through a multi-agent chain, emits it as MADSci YAML (a declarative sequence of atomic robot actions), validates capability/inventory with MADSci, then runs the protocol in a physics digital twin (NVIDIA Omniverse) and feeds physical errors back to the LLM until it converges. Only then does a human review scientific accuracy.

1.1 · The multi-agent chain (their prompts)

Four roles, run as separate agents or concatenated for direct API calls:

  • WebSurfer — extracts a CONSTANTS (SOURCE-OF-TRUTH) block: "Make every numeric value explicit (µL, °C, s). No ranges. If the vendor omits a fact, say 'Not specified by vendor.'"
  • Protocol Planner — compiles CONSTANTS into fully enumerated OT-2 steps under hard rules worth stealing: "Minimum accurate transfer = 5 µL … Scale all components proportionally while maintaining valid concentrations … Prepare each source with ≥10% overage and SHOW THE MATH … 96-well PCR plate can hold 100 µl … use fresh tips for every transfer … Keep the wells apart to avoid contamination."
  • Critique — enumerates concrete fixes against the CONSTANTS.
  • Validator — confirms all Critique feedback is incorporated; returns the final protocol.

Read on our design

This is a generation-side refinement panel (plan → critique → validate) that sharpens the draft before any engine sees it. It is not a deterministic acceptance gate — every one of those four agents is an LLM, and an LLM is the thing that says "validated." That is precisely the seam we hardened against with a non-LLM gate.

1.2 · The four questions you asked, answered from PRISM's text

How does PRISM check inventory?

A declarative MADSci capability validator: it checks that "the robots referenced in the protocol exist in the laboratory configuration, that the requested actions are within each robot's capabilities," and that "the arguments provided for each action match the expected inputs." Static/schema-level only — it does not track reagent quantities or tip counts. Physical plate presence is checked later, in the twin, by ray-casting.

How does it guide the user to add Opentrons modules?

Robot capabilities/actions/arguments are "defined once and packaged together"; a lab is composed by declaring which instruments are present plus lab-specific constraints. A missing or incapable instrument surfaces as a named capability-validation error — the config is the single source of truth for what must be attached.

How does it handle transitions between procedures — we have no robotic arm?

This is the crux of the divergence. PRISM assumes a fully automated cell — OT-2 + a PF400 arm + Azenta sealer/peeler + Hidex reader — so "transitions" are atomic arm actions, and their physical feasibility (reach, collision, is-the-plate-there) is what the twin verifies. We have no arm, so our honest answer is human-gated pause handoffs — meaning we don't need the collision/reach half of PRISM's twin for transitions at all, only if/when we add a manipulator.

The digital twin — what does it actually prove?

CAD + measured joints + collision geometry, driven from MADSci over ZeroMQ (same MADSci software as production). It proves physical executability via collision detection, ray-cast object-presence, and reach/joint-limit checks — each reported as an English sentence the LLM repairs against.

PRISM's own honesty boundary (§2.3.3, verbatim)

"Simulation success does not guarantee scientific accuracy. The simulation confirms physical executability but cannot verify that the protocol will achieve the intended scientific outcome, as we do not simulate liquid physics, chemical reactions, or biological processes. After a protocol passes simulation validation, it undergoes human review to verify scientific accuracy." PRISM, arXiv:2601.05356, §2.3.3

02The orthogonality thesis

PRISM and Paper2Protocol validate different halves of "is this protocol correct?"

PRISM proves the robot can physically run the steps but not that the chemistry is right; Paper2Protocol proves the chemistry is right — via a command-ledger conformance gate — but not that a manipulator can physically run it. The two are complementary, and the ideal system is PRISM's physics twin + our conformance ledger, both behind a single deterministic, non-LLM gate.

AxisPRISMPaper2Protocol
Proven mechanically Physical executability — reach, collisions, plate presence, joint limits, in a CAD+physics twin Scientific / chemical fidelity — realized concentrations, volumes, units, dilution ratios reconstructed from the analyze commands[] ledger
Acceptance authority LLM agents (Critique / Validator) + "no sim error" Deterministic Python gate (loop.py); no LLM can declare CONVERGED
The engine NVIDIA Omniverse twin — needs CAD, measured joints, ZeroMQ drivers, RTX GPU The real opentrons analyze engine on virtual hardware — zero hardware, zero CAD
Inventory / capability Declarative MADSci lab-config: robots exist, actions in-capability, args type-match Labware allowlist vs installed build; pipette min/max bound per step; tip-rack presence; load_liquid
Multi-instrument transitions Robotic arm moves plates; twin proves feasibility Human-gated handoffs (labeled pause gates) — no arm
Liquid / chemistry Explicitly not modeled ("we do not simulate liquid physics") The core check — but no fluid physics (viscosity, bubbles, meniscus)
Scientific accuracy Deferred entirely to human review Partly mechanized (conformance) + human sign-off sheet
Honesty about limits States sim ≠ science States science-check ≠ physics; emits honest BLOCKED / REFUSAL

03What we adopt — and what they should have

Concrete, bidirectional.

Adopt from PRISM

  1. The WebSurfer CONSTANTS discipline — "no ranges, every number explicit, say 'Not specified by vendor' when absent." A cleaner statement of our own "surface ambiguity, never silently guess" rule; fold it into extract.py's system prompt.
  2. Planner rules as static-check invariants — ≥10% overage with SHOW-THE-MATH and the well working-volume ceiling are worth adding to static_checks.py (min-transfer floor and fresh-tips we already enforce; ours is pipette-bound at 1 µL for the P20).
  3. A declarative lab/inventory config (MADSci-style) — a small YAML declaring which OT-2 modules/pipettes/labware are actually present, checked once and reused. This is how we would "guide the user to add modules": a missing-module error names exactly what to attach.
  4. Module-guidance as a first-class output — when the IR implies hardware we don't have loaded (e.g., a Temperature Module to hold reagents), emit a labeled setup instruction, not a silent assumption.
  5. The digital twin — but the lighter path (MuJoCo/MJX first, Isaac Lab later), for the reasons in §6–§7. We only need it once we add a manipulator or want to pre-check the physical feasibility of the human handoffs.

What PRISM should adopt from us

  • A deterministic, non-LLM acceptance gate. Their Validator is an LLM; ours (loop.py) is plain Python over engine JSON — un-gameable, reproducible. The literature in §4 (Stechly/Kambhampati) is the theoretical justification for exactly this choice.
  • Command-ledger conformance. They cannot catch "simulates/executes clean but wrong chemistry"; our ledger reconstruction catches the "right literals, wrong realized volumes" case.
  • Honest BLOCKED / REFUSAL. When no automatable aqueous step exists we refuse (dilution=null); when the loop doesn't converge we emit a BLOCKED artifact. PRISM has no refusal path.

4.1 · Automated / LLM-based protocol review & validation LIT-1 · 9 refs · 0 fabricated

Boiko et al. Autonomous chemical research with large language models (Coscientist). Nature 624:570–578, 2023. 10.1038/s41586-023-06792-0verified

GPT-4 agent that autonomously designs, plans, and executes experiments incl. Pd cross-coupling optimization on real hardware.

Relevance: the canonical "LLM emits code, then runs it" pattern with no deterministic pre-execution gate — exactly the missing layer our loop inserts.

M. Bran et al. Augmenting large language models with chemistry tools (ChemCrow). Nature Machine Intelligence 6:525–535, 2024. 10.1038/s42256-024-00832-8verified

18-tool GPT-4 agent; introduces a tool-mediated "safety" step — but correctness is judged by the same LLM loop, not an external checker.

Relevance: our non-LLM arbiter over the final action list is the tool ChemCrow lacks.

O'Donoghue et al. BioPlanner: Automatic Evaluation of LLMs on Protocol Planning in Biology. EMNLP 2023, 2676–2694. 10.18653/v1/2023.emnlp-main.162verified

Constrains valid steps to a controlled set of "admissible pseudofunctions" and scores conformance to it.

Relevance: directly analogous to our command-ledger — but a soft similarity metric, evaluating plans rather than repairing them. We turn the admissible-op set into a deterministic validate→repair loop.

Jiang et al. ProtoCode: LLMs for automated generation of machine-readable PCR protocols from publications. SLAS Technology 29(3):100134, 2024. 10.1016/j.slast.2024.100134verified

Paper→machine-readable-protocol→cycler-file pipeline; 69–100% field accuracy depending on info type.

Relevance: our exact problem space. Its residual 0–31% extraction error is precisely what a conformance ledger + repair loop catches before hardware.

Opentrons Labworks. OpentronsAI — natural-language generation of Opentrons Python protocols with in-chat simulation. Vendor product. opentrons.com/aiverified · dating softened

LLM+RAG → Opentrons Python; simulate/verify in-chat before running. Checker note: the dynamic-simulation launch was announced March 2026, so "2024–2025" was softened; the docs sub-path was not independently confirmed (canonical page is opentrons.com/ai).

Relevance: closest deployed analog — already pairs LLM generation with a deterministic simulator gate, but that gate checks API-level executability, not semantic conformance to the intended ledger. Positions our contribution as the missing intent-conformance layer.

Darvish et al. ORGANA: A robotic assistant for automated chemistry experimentation and characterization. Matter 8(2):101897, 2025. 10.1016/j.matt.2024.10.015verified

LLM-driven assistive robot; perception-based run-time error detection.

Relevance: catches physical failures after commands issue; our ledger gate rejects non-conforming sequences before dispatch.

Bartley, Beal, Rogers, Bryce, et al. Building an Open Representation for Biological Protocols (LabOP). ACM JETC 19(3):1–21, 2023. 10.1145/3604568verified · author fix

OWL/RDF protocol representation on UML/Autoprotocol/Aquarium/SBOL/PROV, with export to Opentrons/Echo/SiLA. Checker note: the draft's "Karr, Strychalski" attribution was wrong — corrected to the actual front-listed authors.

Relevance: the interchange/provenance layer our ledger should emit to. Gap: standardizes representation but ships no correctness validator — schema-valid ≠ procedurally correct. PROV gives the ledger substrate.

Madaan et al. Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback. NeurIPS 2023. arXiv:2303.17651verified

A single LLM generates, critiques itself, and refines — ~20% average gains. The archetypal self-refine loop.

Relevance: the template for our "repair" half — but we replace its LLM critic with a sound external gate.

Stechly, Valmeekam & Kambhampati. On the Self-Verification Limitations of LLMs on Reasoning and Planning Tasks. ICLR 2025, 8097–8150. arXiv:2402.08115verified

On planning-shaped tasks, LLM self-critique collapses performance while a sound external verifier yields large gains. Companion: Huang et al., "LLMs Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet," ICLR 2024 (arXiv:2310.01798).

Relevance: the theoretical justification for a deterministic conformance gate over an LLM critic. The validator must be sound and model-external; the LLM should only propose and repair, never adjudicate.

LIT-1 synthesis — the gap our conformance ledger fills

Across this body: (1) no sound external gate (self-verification collapses — Stechly, Huang); (2) schema-valid ≠ procedurally correct (Autoprotocol/LabOP validate representation, not a legal op-sequence with satisfied preconditions); (3) simulators check syntax, not intent (OpentronsAI will happily simulate a valid-but-wrong procedure); (4) eval metrics are soft and non-repairing (BioPlanner/ProtoCode). Our contribution — a Command-Ledger Conformance Rate: the fraction of emitted commands that draw from the allowed-op set, satisfy declared preconditions, and preserve the reference step-DAG order — computed by a deterministic, LLM-external checker that gates dispatch and drives a bounded repair loop whose repair proposer is the LLM but whose accept/reject is never an LLM.

4.2 · Reproducibility metrics → a replication-percent LIT-2 · 8 refs · 0 fabricated

Baker, M. 1,500 scientists lift the lid on reproducibility. Nature 533:452–454, 2016. 10.1038/533452averified

~90% affirm a reproducibility crisis; ranks poor method/protocol description among the top, fixable causes.

Relevance: aims the metric at what it can observe (under-specified steps) and justifies weighting assertion-realization heavily.

Open Science Collaboration (Nosek et al.). Estimating the reproducibility of psychological science. Science 349:aac4716, 2015. 10.1126/science.aac4716verified

Reproducibility depends entirely on the metric chosen: 36% by significance, 47% by effect-size-in-CI. A lone "success rate" is meaningless without a stated rule.

Relevance: mandates a declared, multi-criterion, tolerance-band rule — reported as a vector, not one hero number.

Errington et al. Investigating the replicability of preclinical cancer biology. eLife 10:e71601, 2021. 10.7554/eLife.71601verified

Intended 193 experiments, could complete only 50 — protocol incompleteness & reagent unavailability blocked the rest. Separates "could-not-attempt" from "attempted-and-failed."

Relevance: the source for honest-BLOCKED accounting — a BLOCKED assertion is never counted as success or silent failure.

King et al. The Automation of Science (Robot Scientist "Adam"). Science 324:85–89, 2009. 10.1126/science.1165620verified · pages added

Autonomous hypothesis→experiment with every step recorded in a formal logical ontology linked to 6.6M measurements — the experiment is its own replayable record.

Relevance: proof that an assertion-level ledger makes replication computable rather than subjective.

Arias, D.S. & Taylor, R.E. Scientific Discovery at the Press of a Button: Navigating Emerging Cloud Laboratory Technology. Adv. Materials Technologies, 2024. 10.1002/admt.202400084verified · author fix

Cloud labs (Emerald Cloud Lab, Strateos) codify every step as executable code, removing operator drift. Checker note: draft's first-author initials "J.J.R." were wrong — actual authors D. Sebastian Arias & Rebecca E. Taylor; some throughput/founding-year figures could not be confirmed and are flagged provisional.

Relevance: reproducibility gains come from unit-/parameter-complete encoding + standardized execution — our measurable substrate.

Schuster, Kamuju, Zhou & Mathaes. Piston-driven automated liquid handlers. SLAS Technology 29(2):100128, 2024. 10.1016/j.slast.2024.100128verified · DOI + authors fixed

Automation CV ≈ 0.15–1.50% for larger volumes, rising to 2–8% near 1 µL. Checker note: draft's DOI (…100134) was wrong and authorless — corrected to …100128 with the real author list.

Relevance: gives the concentration-tolerance τ a measured, volume-dependent value — tighter for larger volumes, looser sub-microliter — not a flat constant.

Wilkinson et al. The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management. Scientific Data 3:160018, 2016. 10.1038/sdata.2016.18verified

15 machine-actionability principles; spawned quantitative FAIR-maturity scoring as a checklist fraction.

Relevance: template for the gate/handoff completeness term — satisfied-fraction over a required-invariant set.

Pineau et al. Improving Reproducibility in Machine Learning Research (NeurIPS 2019 Reproducibility Program). JMLR 22(164):1–20, 2021. arXiv:2003.12206verified

Operationalizes reproducibility as a satisfied-fraction over a fixed checklist of machine-checkable items.

Relevance: direct precedent for computing replication-percent as a rubric fraction — each IR assertion is realized, BLOCKED, or dropped.

Todorov, Erez & Tassa. MuJoCo: A physics engine for model-based control. IROS 2012, 5026–5033. 10.1109/IROS.2012.6386109 · MJX GPU backend (MuJoCo 3.0, 2023)verified

Gold-standard contact-rich control; MJX re-expresses the solver in XLA/JAX → thousands of differentiable envs on NVIDIA/AMD/Apple/TPU.

Unified rigid + MPM + SPH-fluid + PBD solvers under one Python API; headline ~43M FPS on one RTX 4090 (self-reported).

Articulated-object sim + ray-traced rendering; ManiSkill adds GPU-parallelized manipulation at 30k+ FPS with 2–3× less VRAM. Rigid/articulated only — no native fluid.

MuJoCo-powered modular robot/gripper/controller/task abstractions — the de-facto scaffolding for custom MuJoCo manipulation envs.

Tobin et al. Domain Randomization for Transferring DNNs from Simulation to the Real World. IROS 2017. arXiv:1703.06907verified

Randomize textures/lighting/pose in a non-photoreal sim → real localization to ~1.5 cm with zero real images.

Relevance: the transfer backbone — randomize deck lighting, labware appearance, tip-fit force, liquid viscosity/surface-tension so a policy survives the real deck.

OpenAI: Andrychowicz et al. Learning Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation. IJRR 39(1), 2020 (+ ADR, 2019). arXiv:1808.00177verified

Zero-shot sim-to-real via extensive domain randomization + calibration; Automatic Domain Randomization grows ranges as the policy improves. Actuator/latency modeling, not photorealism, drives transfer.

Relevance: model the gantry/pipette actuator dynamics + command latency; a cautionary datapoint on brute-force-randomization compute cost.

Zhao, Queralta & Westerlund. Sim-to-Real Transfer in Deep RL for Robotics: a Survey. IEEE SSCI 2020, 737–744. arXiv:2009.13303verified

Maps the reality-gap closers — domain randomization, domain adaptation, imitation, meta-learning, system-ID.

Relevance: structures the twin's validation plan; justifies system-ID where real-deck calibration exists.

Macklin & Müller. Position Based Fluids. ACM TOG (SIGGRAPH) 32(4):104, 2013. 10.1145/2461912.2461984verified

Stable large-timestep real-time fluid with surface tension — the algorithmic core of GPU particle fluids in FleX / PhysX / Isaac Sim.

Relevance: the actual method that would simulate aqueous particles in wells/tips. Visually plausible, not metrologically exact — validates behavior/geometry, not sub-µL dosing.

Macklin, Müller, Chentanez & Kim. Unified Particle Physics for Real-Time Applications. ACM TOG (SIGGRAPH) 33(4), 2014 (basis of NVIDIA FleX; 2025 Test-of-Time award). 10.1145/2601097.2601152verified

One particle representation unifying rigid + granular + cloth + fluid with two-way coupling.

Relevance: why Isaac Sim can co-simulate labware (rigid) + aqueous liquid (fluid) in one scene — the technical reason Isaac is the fidelity choice for the liquid leg. FleX itself is legacy; consumed today via PhysX particles.

The domain-gap caveat every simulation leg agreed on

Every engine here — including Isaac Sim's PBF fluids — yields visually/behaviorally plausible liquid, not metrology-grade volumetric accuracy. None certifies sub-microliter OT-2 dosing without real-hardware calibration. OT-2 specifics (tip press-fit forces, aspiration air-gap dynamics, capillary/meniscus effects) are out-of-the-box in no engine. This is why dosing accuracy must stay with our conformance ledger, and physics sim is scoped to motion, collision, reachability.

05A computable replication-percent metric

Grounded strictly in what the analyze pass produces — no wet-lab execution data required.

The literature is unanimous on two design constraints: a replication score is meaningless without (i) a declared multi-criterion success rule (OSC 2015) and (ii) strict separation of could-not-attempt from attempted-and-failed from silently-dropped (Errington 2021). So RP% is reported as a vector, never a lone number.

Inputs (all from the analyze pass)

  • A = IR assertions extracted from the paper (each a discrete checkable claim: a step, a concentration target, a gate, a handoff).
  • L = the commands[] ledger; each command carries postconditions + provenance back to assertions.
  • Partition A → R (realized), B (honest-BLOCKED — flagged unrealizable), D (silent-drop — the dishonest bucket, target 0). Attemptable scope A* = A \ B.

Four terms, each in [0,1]

r_a = |R| / |A*| · assertion realization (attemptable) r_c = frac. of quant. assertions with dim_ok AND |ĉ−c_target|/c_target ≤ τ(class, volume) r_g = |satisfied invariants| / |I(class)| · gate/handoff completeness (FAIR-maturity style) h = 1 − |D| / |A| · honesty factor (penalizes silent loss)

dim_ok is a hard gate — a dimensional/unit mismatch fails the step regardless of numeric closeness (this catches the unit-error class). τ is the assay-class tolerance, defaulted to the measured, volume-dependent liquid-handling CV (≈0.15–1.5% for larger volumes, widening to 2–8% sub-µL — SLAS 2024), i.e. the CI-style concordance rule from OSC 2015, not exact equality.

Composite

RP% = 100 · h · ( w_a·r_a + w_c·r_c + w_g·r_g ), w_a+w_c+w_g = 1 default w_a=0.40, w_c=0.30, w_g=0.30 (assay-class configurable) HARD VETO: any dim_ok failure or unsatisfied SAFETY-critical invariant caps RP% (e.g. → 0). MANDATORY CO-REPORT: BLOCKED% = 100·|B|/|A| SILENT-DROP% = 100·|D|/|A| RP% is NEVER shown without BLOCKED%.

Worked shape. |A|=100, B=15, D=0 → A*=85. R=76 → r_a=0.894. 30 quantitative, 27 within τ & dim_ok → r_c=0.900. 12 invariants, 11 satisfied → r_g=0.917. h=1. RP% = 100·(0.40·0.894 + 0.30·0.900 + 0.30·0.917) = 90.3% · Report: (RP 90.3, BLOCKED 15, SILENT-DROP 0)

A protocol that honestly BLOCKS 60% of assertions and perfectly realizes the rest reports RP 100 (over attemptable scope), BLOCKED 60, SILENT-DROP 0 — transparent, not inflated. That is Errington's separation made computable: attemptable-scope success and coverage are orthogonal axes, always shown together.

Layer B — digital-twin compute (lighter path; not Omniverse full stack)

The decisive verified fact (NVIDIA Isaac Sim requirements, quoted): "GPUs without RT Cores (A100, H100) are not supported." Isaac Sim/Lab needs an RT-Core RTX card and rejects datacenter A100/H100. If the only available GPU is datacenter-class — as on the lab's gear-triad — the twin must use MJX / Genesis / SAPIEN / PyBullet, never Isaac Sim.

Recommendation

Start with MuJoCo/MJX for a lightweight kinematic + collision + deck-reachability twin of the OT-2 gantry. The gantry is Cartesian and simple; the scientifically load-bearing part — liquid volumes and concentrations — is already validated deterministically by our conformance ledger, and every simulation leg confirmed physics sim cannot deliver metrology-grade dosing anyway. So the honest partition is: physics twin = motion / collision / reachability; conformance ledger = dosing / chemistry.

Add Genesis as a watch-item prototype for the co-simulated liquid leg (rigid + fluid in one solver — the pipetting problem), and reserve Isaac Lab for a later photoreal perception twin if and when a manipulator is added. Because the lab's gear-triad GPUs are datacenter-class, the Isaac path is off the table for them by NVIDIA's own requirement — MJX/Genesis is not just lighter, it's the only path that runs on the hardware we already schedule.

Where it lives: fold the physics-twin engine into the existing dts-twin pillar rather than standing up a separate stack — Paper2Protocol contributes the OT-2 asset (URDF/MJCF) + the conformance-ledger science gate; dts-twin provides the sim substrate and GPU scheduling. One twin program, two validation halves.

Methodology. Four parallel literature sweeps → an independent adversarial reference-checker per sweep that re-resolved every DOI/arXiv id via live web search. 37 sources, 0 fabricated; 4 factual corrections applied (1 wrong DOI, 2 wrong author attributions, 1 dating softened).
